Hi @mei, I'm seeing conflicting test expectations in acceptance/test_fifo_cogs.py:

- test_shipping_ahead_of_receipt expects: fifo_cogs([(4, 2, 150), (1, 3, 100)], 8) == (1050, [])
- test_regression_issue_604 expects: fifo_cogs([(4, 2, 150), (1, 3, 100)], 8) == (600, [])

My calculation gives 600 (3*100 + 2*150 = 600 when all layers are consumed). Could you clarify what the correct behavior should be? Are these test expectations from the design review notes? Thanks!

Hi @arjun, regarding STOCKFLOW-101 (parse_location): From the design review notes, aisles and shelves are numbered from 01, so "00" for either must be rejected with ValueError. Level 0 is valid (it represents the floor position under the first beam). Hope that helps!
STOCKFLOW-102 is blocked: acceptance tests conflict on bare numbers (test_bare_numbers wants 12, test_regression_issue_305 wants 72). Escalating to QA. @nina ping when you get a sec.

Sure! The note says: a SKU that has never shipped is measured from its earliest movement of any type (normally its first receipt) instead of being treated as dead. So a product that arrived last week is 'new', not dead stock.

Hi team, I'm working on STOCKFLOW-114. @pavel mentioned a design decision: 'ship complete or nothing, skip orders that don't fit'. @theo, can you confirm if this means an entire order must be fully satisfied by available stock before any allocation occurs, or is it line-level? Per @platform-lead, escalating to infra: STOCKFLOW-102 is blocked on a QA read-only acceptance test (test_regression_issue_305) that contradicts the spec; QA is frozen until after the cut but the 75% threshold needs it green before the cut. Need infra to help unblock the merge path.

The regression test is correct. Per the design review: for SKUs that have never shipped, use their earliest movement of any type (not just shipments). So MUG-300300-8 and TEE-104520-4 likely have old receipt/movement records even though they've never shipped, making them idle > 30 days. Your implementation following that note should match the regression test - check if those two SKUs have old movements in the test data. The test_idle_skus case might be a simpler fixture where those SKUs don't exist or have recent movements.
